meta.label: Pensions & investing
meta.attribution: Curated from public fund characteristics, fossil-free screening, and holdings transparency - not audited data, and NOT financial advice. Your pension and investments are often the biggest 'vote' your money casts; always read the actual holdings/prospectus and consider an adviser. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare pensions & investing by environmental impact, fees, labor and sourcing, and disclosure.

axes.label: Fees or overall fit
axes.question: Lower fees or a stronger overall fit?

consumer.axes: Round 8 practical decision dials, with the S4 cost-or-values default where evidence permits.
consumer.budget: Round 8 honest budget eligibility, with S4 refusing to guess missing cost data.
consumer.archetypes: Round 8 computed answer slots matched to available category evidence.
consumer.page: Round 7 personal precedence extended in Round 9 to the shared decision page for every live category.

products.name: Fossil-free index fund / ETF
products.description: A passive fund or ETF that tracks a broad market index while excluding companies with fossil-fuel reserves or related screens.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds is built to check fund holdings for fossil-fuel exposure; fossil-free index ETFs use this same holdings-screen logic.

ethics.note: As You Sow's Invest Your Values tools extend fund checks beyond fossil fuels to screens such as weapons, prisons, tobacco and gender/racial justice.

transparency.note: Passive funds and ETFs publish prospectuses and holdings; the user still has to check the actual fund, not the label.

fees.note: Index funds generally carry lower costs than active funds because they track an index rather than pay for active selection.

accessibility.note: ETFs are traded through brokerage accounts, but pension-platform availability depends on the plan or provider.

products.name: Triodos / ethical-bank funds
products.description: Impact funds from an ethical-bank group that publishes investment philosophy, exclusions, and fund documentation.

environment.note: Triodos describes its investment management as investing in the transition themes it considers sustainable and future-fit.

ethics.note: Triodos states minimum standards and positive impact criteria for what its funds can and cannot finance.

transparency.note: Triodos publishes fund pages and annual reports with portfolio and impact information for its investment funds.

fees.note: Triodos funds are active impact funds; costs must be checked in each fund's KID/prospectus rather than assumed cheap.

accessibility.note: Triodos investment funds are offered in selected European markets, so availability is narrower than global ETFs.

products.name: Green bonds / climate bonds
products.description: Debt instruments whose proceeds are intended for green or climate-related projects, usually accessed through bond funds or platforms.

environment.note: The Climate Bonds Standard certifies bonds against sector criteria intended to align financing with climate goals.

ethics.note: Green-bond impact depends on the issuer and use of proceeds; labelled bonds are project-linked rather than automatically ethical.

transparency.note: Green Bond Principles expect use-of-proceeds disclosure and reporting, but reporting quality still varies.

fees.note: Costs depend on whether you buy bonds directly or through a fund; fund fees are disclosed in fund documents.

accessibility.note: Most retail investors access diversified green bonds through funds or platforms rather than single project bonds.

products.name: Community investing (CDFI / credit union)
products.description: Community-development investing that puts capital into local lending, housing, small business, and underserved communities.

environment.note: CDFIs are not automatically climate-screened, but their mission is community development rather than fossil extraction or sector speculation.

ethics.note: The CDFI Fund certifies mission-driven institutions that serve low-income and underserved communities.

transparency.note: Certified CDFIs are listed by the CDFI Fund, but individual impact reporting varies by institution.

fees.note: Returns and fees vary widely by note, deposit, fund, or credit-union product; this is not a single standardized fee product.

accessibility.note: Availability is usually local, membership-based, or platform-specific rather than a one-click default in every brokerage.

products.name: Green Century Funds
products.description: A US mutual-fund family built around fossil-fuel-free environmental screens and shareholder advocacy.

environment.note: Green Century states that its mutual funds are fossil fuel free and avoid companies exploring for, extracting, processing, refining, or transmitting fossil fuels.

ethics.note: Green Century describes an environmental-advocacy model including shareholder advocacy and ownership by nonprofit environmental groups.

transparency.note: Green Century publishes fund pages, prospectuses, shareholder reports, tickers and holdings documents.

fees.note: Green Century's FAQ lists individual-share expense ratios around 1.20%-1.47%, much higher than broad passive index funds.

accessibility.note: US retail mutual funds with stated minimums and account workflows; not a default workplace plan for most people.

products.name: Domini Impact Investments
products.description: A US impact-investing mutual-fund manager with explicit social and environmental standards.

environment.note: Domini's standards exclude fossil fuels in core impact strategies, though Fossil Free Funds should still be used fund-by-fund.

ethics.note: Domini publishes impact investment standards covering human dignity and ecological sustainability.

transparency.note: Domini publishes fund pages and documents, including prospectuses and shareholder materials.

fees.note: Domini is an active impact manager; expenses must be read in the specific fund prospectus and are not index-fund-low by default.

accessibility.note: Domini mutual funds are US-focused retail funds, available through selected platforms rather than every pension default.

products.name: Calvert Impact Community Investment Note
products.description: A fixed-income community-investment note that channels capital to mission-driven organizations.

environment.note: Calvert Impact's reports page lists a Q1 2026 Community Investment Note report, keeping the note's impact and environmental portfolio trail current.

ethics.note: Calvert Impact's current reports trail frames the Community Investment Note around community, inclusive-finance and mission-driven portfolio partners.

transparency.note: Calvert Impact publishes recurring Community Investment Note reports, including a Q1 2026 report listed in its report library.

fees.note: This is not a mutual-fund expense-ratio product; investors must read the current note reports, rates, terms and risk documents carefully.

accessibility.note: A specialized note with term and risk considerations remains more work than choosing a standard mutual fund or ETF.

products.name: Sustainable target-date fund
products.description: A one-fund retirement option that adds sustainability or ESG tilts to a target-date glide path.

environment.note: BlackRock's LifePath ESG Index example applies ESG index exposures, but this is a tilt rather than strict fossil-free exclusion.

ethics.note: SEC guidance warns that ESG funds can define and weigh ESG factors very differently, so target-date ESG is not automatically strict impact investing.

transparency.note: Target-date fund pages disclose objective, holdings, documents and sustainability characteristics, but users still need to check underlying holdings.

fees.note: Index-based target-date structures are usually cheaper than active impact funds, but each share class has its own expense ratio.

accessibility.note: Target-date funds are designed as retirement-account defaults, so they often fit workplace-plan workflows better than assembling several funds.

products.name: Robo-advisor sustainable portfolio
products.description: An automated portfolio that selects screened ETFs for people who want a simple hands-off investing workflow.

environment.note: Betterment's SRI portfolios use ESG-screened ETFs, but the strength of fossil and social screens depends on the underlying ETFs.

ethics.note: Robo SRI portfolios are screened portfolios, not bespoke impact mandates; SEC warns ESG strategies vary widely.

transparency.note: Robo-advisors generally disclose the ETFs used, but users must inspect those ETFs for actual holdings.

fees.note: Automated portfolios add an advisory fee on top of ETF expenses, usually below full-service advice but above DIY.

accessibility.note: The main advantage is usability: automated allocation, rebalancing and low-minimum workflows.

products.name: Betterment Climate Impact portfolio
products.description: A robo-advisor portfolio tilted toward fossil-fuel-reserve-free equity funds and green-bond exposure for climate-conscious investors.

environment.note: Betterment says its Climate Impact portfolio uses fossil-fuel-reserve-free funds and bonds that fund green projects.

ethics.note: The portfolio has a stronger environmental focus than all-ESG social screening, so social and governance fit depends on the underlying ETFs.

transparency.note: Betterment publishes its Climate Impact methodology and lists the role of the funds used, but investors still need to inspect the ETFs themselves.

fees.note: Betterment's investing advice starts at a 0.25% annual advisory fee or a monthly fee for some small balances, plus underlying fund expenses.

accessibility.note: The portfolio is designed for Betterment automated-investing users, making it easier than building and rebalancing a climate portfolio manually.

products.name: Wealthfront Socially Responsible portfolio
products.description: A robo-advisor SRI portfolio using ESG-aware ETFs, built for easy automated investing rather than strict divestment.

environment.note: Wealthfront's SRI methodology uses ESG-aware funds selected for factors such as carbon emissions, diversity and board composition, not strict fossil-free exclusion.

ethics.note: Wealthfront says the portfolio is designed around sustainability, diversity, equity and more, but uses mainstream ESG-aware ETFs as building blocks.

transparency.note: Wealthfront publishes portfolio holdings and a whitepaper explaining its SRI construction methodology.

fees.note: Wealthfront lists a 0.25% annual advisory fee for Automated Investing, in addition to fund expense ratios.

accessibility.note: The portfolio is available to automated-investing clients and can be selected during sign-up, making the workflow easy for hands-off investors.

products.name: Your pension's ethical/sustainable fund
products.description: The sustainable or ethical fund already offered inside an employer pension, retirement plan, or pension provider menu.

environment.note: Make My Money Matter argues that pensions can finance climate harm or solutions; check the specific fund's fossil exposure.

ethics.note: Workplace sustainable options vary from strict exclusions to light ESG tilts, so the scheme document matters.

transparency.note: Fund factsheets and annual reports should disclose objectives, top holdings and fees; do not rely on the word 'ethical' alone.

fees.note: Workplace-plan fees can be similar to defaults or materially different; read the scheme's fund factsheet.

accessibility.note: The practical advantage is that the fund may already be available inside the pension you use today.

products.name: Vanguard FTSE Social Index Fund
products.description: A large, low-cost US social index fund that applies FTSE exclusionary screens while staying broad and easy to buy.

environment.note: The 2026 Vanguard fact sheet says FTSE excludes companies involved in selected activities and those failing labor, human-rights, environmental, anti-corruption or diversity standards.

ethics.note: The fund is screened, but it remains a broad public-equity index product rather than a deep impact or shareholder-advocacy strategy.

transparency.note: Vanguard publishes fund profile, fact sheet, prospectus and holdings information for the FTSE Social Index Fund.

fees.note: Vanguard lists a 0.11% expense ratio for VFTAX as of 02/02/2026, much cheaper than active impact funds.

accessibility.note: A large Vanguard mutual fund is relatively accessible through US brokerage and retirement-platform workflows, though minimums and plan menus still matter.

products.name: Fidelity U.S. Sustainability Index Fund (FITLX)
products.description: A low-cost US mutual fund tracking an MSCI USA ESG index, useful as a mainstream screened-index option but not a strict impact fund.

environment.note: Fidelity says FITLX seeks to track the MSCI USA ESG Index, which targets US companies with high ESG characteristics, not a fossil-free-only screen.

ethics.note: The fund is a broad ESG index product, so social-screen strength depends on the MSCI index method and underlying holdings.

transparency.note: Fidelity publishes a fund profile with objective, holdings, ratings, risk and document links for FITLX.

fees.note: Fidelity's index-fund comparison lists FITLX at a 0.110% expense ratio, competitive with Vanguard's social index fund.

accessibility.note: A Fidelity mutual fund is straightforward for US brokerage investors, though workplace retirement availability still depends on plan menus.

products.name: Vanguard ESG International Stock ETF (VSGX)
products.description: A low-cost international stock ETF with ESG screens, filling the non-US side of a simple screened portfolio.

environment.note: VSGX tracks a screened international benchmark, but Fossil Free Funds still reports fossil exposure, so it is ESG-screened rather than fossil-free.

ethics.note: Vanguard says the fund screens developed and emerging-market companies for certain ESG criteria, not a deep social-impact mandate.

transparency.note: Vanguard publishes objective, performance, expense, holdings and risk details for VSGX.

fees.note: Vanguard's workplace profile lists a 0.10% expense ratio for VSGX as of 12/19/2025.

accessibility.note: A US-listed Vanguard ETF is easy to buy through many brokerages, though it may be absent from employer retirement menus.

products.name: Sphere 500 Climate Fund (SPFFX)
products.description: A fossil-free US large-cap mutual fund designed to fit 401(k) menus with a low net expense ratio and climate-aligned voting.

environment.note: Sphere says its index starts with the top 500 US companies and removes fossil-fuel and other excluded companies using As You Sow data.

ethics.note: The index excludes fossil fuel, deforestation, tobacco, civilian firearm, military weapon and private-prison companies, though fossil finance exposure can remain.

transparency.note: Sphere publishes fund, index, fee, platform and risk disclosures; Fossil Free Funds provides an independent holdings screen.

fees.note: Sphere says investors pay a 0.07% net expense ratio despite a higher gross expense ratio, aiming to make the fund suitable for 401(k)s.

accessibility.note: Sphere says the fund is designed for existing 401(k) plans and can be invested in through platforms such as Vanguard, Fidelity and Schwab, but plan adoption still matters.

products.name: Parnassus Core Equity Fund
products.description: A long-running US responsible-investing mutual fund that combines ESG analysis with a conventional large-cap equity mandate.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds reports no direct fossil-fuel stock holdings for Parnassus Core Equity, while noting fossil finance/insurance exposure keeps it at a B tier.

ethics.note: Parnassus says its strategies evaluate ESG factors as part of the investment decision-making process.

transparency.note: Parnassus publishes a fund page, full holdings and fund documents for Core Equity.

fees.note: Parnassus lists a 0.81% net expense ratio for investor shares, materially above low-cost passive index funds.

accessibility.note: The fund is open to US mutual-fund investors, but active-fund pricing and platform availability make it less frictionless than a broad ETF.

products.name: Adasina Social Justice All Cap Global ETF
products.description: A diversified ETF built around community-sourced social-justice criteria, with strong screens but mixed holding-level social scorecards.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds reports JSTC data from a Nov. 30, 2025 N-PORT filing: 0.19% fossil-fuel stock exposure and no fossil-finance or fossil-insurance holdings flagged.

ethics.note: Adasina's criteria cover racial, gender, economic and climate justice, but As You Sow rates JSTC D on gender, diversity disclosure and racial-justice holdings.

transparency.note: Adasina publishes prospectus links, quarterly holdings, performance data and daily holding snapshots on the fund page.

fees.note: Adasina lists a 0.89% expense ratio for JSTC, far above plain broad-market index ETFs.

accessibility.note: JSTC is a NYSE-listed ETF, making it brokerage-accessible, but its specialized mandate may not appear in ordinary workplace pension menus.

products.name: Nia Impact Solutions Fund
products.description: A women-led impact mutual fund with fossil-free and solution-theme strengths, tempered by mixed holding-level social scorecards.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds reports $0 in fossil-fuel investments and 0% of assets flagged for NIAGX as of the 2025 N-PORT filing.

ethics.note: Nia's prospectus uses six solution themes and diversity criteria, but As You Sow rates NIAGX D on gender, diversity disclosure and racial-justice holdings.

transparency.note: Nia publishes holdings, annual and semiannual reports, prospectus, fact sheet and proxy-voting documents on the fund site.

fees.note: Fidelity's current fund summary shows 1.38% gross expenses and 0.98% net expenses for NIAGX, still materially above cheap index ETFs.

accessibility.note: Nia says NIAGX is available with minimums as low as $1,000 at platforms such as Fidelity and Schwab, but it remains less universal than broad ETFs.

products.name: iShares Global Clean Energy ETF
products.description: A mainstream clean-energy ETF tracking global companies involved in the clean-energy transition, with sector concentration risk.

environment.note: BlackRock says ICLN tracks an index of global companies involved in clean energy and applies business-involvement screens for several fossil and weapons categories.

ethics.note: The fund is climate-themed, not a broad social-justice screen; the business screens do not make every holding labor- or governance-leading.

transparency.note: BlackRock publishes index, holdings, expense ratio and sustainability screen information for ICLN.

fees.note: BlackRock lists a 0.39% expense ratio, cheaper than many active impact funds but above the cheapest broad-market ETFs.

accessibility.note: A large NASDAQ-listed iShares ETF is easy to buy through many brokerages, though thematic concentration is not a default retirement allocation.

products.name: Trillium ESG Global Equity Fund
products.description: An active global equity fund from a long-running responsible-investing manager, with ESG integration and screening.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds reports 2.15% of assets in fossil-fuel stocks for the Trillium ESG Global Equity Fund, giving it a B fossil-fuel grade.

ethics.note: Trillium says the fund invests in companies it believes are leaders in managing environmental, social and governance risks and opportunities.

transparency.note: Trillium publishes strategy, fund documents and holdings materials, but the active ESG process still requires trust in the manager's judgment.

fees.note: Active global ESG mutual funds usually cost materially more than broad passive index funds; read the current documents before buying.

accessibility.note: A US mutual fund is easier than private impact investing, but less universally available than broad ETFs or pension defaults.

products.name: Vanguard ESG U.S. Stock ETF (ESGV)
products.description: A low-cost US ETF that tracks a broad ESG-screened benchmark, useful as an accessible screened alternative to an unscreened total-market fund.

environment.note: Vanguard says ESGV seeks to track a benchmark screened for certain environmental, social and corporate-governance criteria, not a deep impact mandate.

ethics.note: The prospectus describes broad US equity exposure screened for ESG criteria; the investment objective can be changed without shareholder approval.

transparency.note: Vanguard publishes a profile, prospectus, price/performance data and holdings materials for the ETF.

fees.note: Vanguard lists ESGV as a low-cost ETF; the profile shows the current expense-ratio context.

accessibility.note: A US-listed ETF is broadly accessible through brokerage accounts, though employer retirement menus may not include it.

products.name: iShares ESG Aware MSCI USA ETF (ESGU)
products.description: A large, mainstream ESG-aware US equity ETF: easy to buy and transparent, but closer to light ESG tilting than full fossil-free or impact investing.

environment.note: The iShares page showed 3.42% energy-sector exposure as of Jun 23, 2026, so ESGU is ESG-aware rather than fossil-free.

ethics.note: BlackRock says the fund targets ESG considerations in a core US equity portfolio while seeking similar risk and return to the MSCI USA Index.

transparency.note: iShares publishes daily holdings and exposure breakdowns, making the light-screen nature inspectable.

fees.note: The iShares fact sheet lists a 0.15% expense ratio, cheaper than most active ESG funds but above the cheapest plain index ETFs.

accessibility.note: A large US-listed iShares ETF is easy to buy through many brokerages, separate from whether a workplace plan offers it.

products.name: SPDR S&P 500 Fossil Fuel Reserves Free ETF (SPYX)
products.description: A US S&P 500-style ETF that excludes companies owning fossil-fuel reserves, giving a clearer climate screen than generic ESG labels.

environment.note: State Street says SPYX tracks an index designed to eliminate companies that own fossil-fuel reserves from the S&P 500.

ethics.note: The screen is climate/reserves-specific rather than a broad social, labor, weapons, prisons or democracy screen.

transparency.note: State Street publishes daily holdings, sector allocations and fund documents for SPYX.

fees.note: State Street listed a 0.20% gross expense ratio for SPYX in June 2026.

accessibility.note: State Street notes ETF shares can be bought and sold through brokerage accounts on major US exchanges.

products.name: TCW Transform 500 ETF (VOTE)
products.description: A broad US large-cap ETF, formerly Engine No. 1 Transform 500, built around shareholder voting and engagement rather than exclusionary screening.

environment.note: VOTE's model is active ownership inside broad equity exposure, so it can hold high-impact companies while trying to influence them.

ethics.note: Engine No. 1 says voting is a key lever for transparency and sustainable-business governance at large companies.

transparency.note: The SEC filing identifies TCW Transform 500 ETF (ticker VOTE) and its ETF trust structure; the active-ownership claim still depends on voting records.

fees.note: The SEC filing states a 0.05% annual management-fee rate for the Transform 500 ETF.

accessibility.note: As an ETF listed under ticker VOTE, access is brokerage-based and easier than private stewardship products, but narrower than major index giants.

products.name: Dimensional US Sustainability Core 1 ETF (DFSU)
products.description: A low-cost US equity ETF that tilts toward sustainability characteristics, but is not a fully fossil-free fund.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds reports DFSU as having some fossil-fuel exposure, so it earns credit for sustainability tilt but not full fossil-free status.

ethics.note: Dimensional presents DFSU as a US core equity ETF using sustainability considerations inside a diversified equity process.

transparency.note: The fund page publishes portfolio, performance, documents and expense information, making the actual strategy inspectable.

fees.note: Dimensional lists DFSU as a low-expense ETF relative to many active sustainability products.

accessibility.note: As a listed ETF, DFSU is generally brokerage-accessible, though availability depends on country, account type and platform.

products.name: Nuveen Large Cap Responsible Equity Fund
products.description: A large US responsible-equity fund with explicit ESG guidelines and comparatively low institutional share-class fees.

environment.note: Nuveen says the fund includes only holdings deemed consistent with its ESG guidelines, reducing the eligible universe versus an unscreened fund.

ethics.note: Responsible investing is central to the fund's mandate, but values fit still depends on the specific Nuveen guidelines and holdings.

transparency.note: Nuveen publishes portfolio characteristics, holdings, documents, risks and expenses on the fund page.

fees.note: The R6-style share classes shown by Nuveen are priced much lower than many active responsible mutual funds, though share-class access varies.

accessibility.note: The fund is available in multiple share classes, often through retirement plans or brokerage platforms rather than as a simple one-click ETF.

products.name: Brown Advisory Sustainable Growth Fund
products.description: An active US sustainable-growth fund that looks for sustainability-linked business advantages, with stronger intent but higher fees than passive ETFs.

environment.note: Brown Advisory says the strategy evaluates sustainable investment risks and opportunities as part of company selection.

ethics.note: Brown Advisory's current fund page cautions that investors may differ on whether holdings reflect their values, so this is not a pure exclusion fund.

transparency.note: The fund page publishes performance, holdings, factsheets and prospectus materials.

fees.note: Brown Advisory reports materially higher expenses than low-cost index ETFs, which matters for long-term investors.

accessibility.note: The mutual fund is available through selected brokerage and adviser channels, but less frictionless than a broad ETF.

products.name: Mirova Global Sustainable Equity Fund
products.description: A global sustainable-equity strategy with detailed impact reporting, but high costs and platform availability that varies by market.

environment.note: Natixis' current Mirova fund page describes a multi-thematic sustainable-equity approach and lists current holdings and impact-report documents.

ethics.note: The fund invests around sustainable investment themes, but investors still need to review holdings for their own exclusion thresholds.

transparency.note: Natixis lists current Mirova fund documents, including factsheets, holdings reports, a quarterly impact report, and the annual impact report.

fees.note: Natixis fund details show ongoing costs materially above low-cost index ETFs, making fees a real tradeoff.

accessibility.note: Availability depends on share class, investor type and platform, so access is narrower than major US-listed ETFs.

products.name: Impax Global Environmental Markets Fund
products.description: An active global equity fund focused on companies positioned for environmental markets, with strong impact reporting but active-fund costs.

environment.note: Impax frames the strategy around companies benefiting from the transition to a more sustainable economy.

ethics.note: The strategy is environmentally thematic rather than a universal ethical screen, so social-values fit depends on holdings and exclusions.

transparency.note: Impax publishes fund pages, reports and Beyond Financial Returns materials for the strategy.

fees.note: The fund flyer reports active mutual-fund expense ratios far above broad passive ETFs.

accessibility.note: The US fund materials describe specific US share classes and platform-dependent retail access, so this is not a truly global product.

products.name: Calvert US Large-Cap Core Responsible Index ETF
products.description: A responsible-index ETF for US large-cap exposure, stronger than a plain index on values screens but still broad-market in character.

environment.note: Calvert says the ETF gives exposure to companies it believes manage key environmental, social and governance risks and opportunities effectively.

ethics.note: The index uses Calvert Principles for Responsible Investment, but remains a large-cap index product rather than a targeted impact fund.

transparency.note: The Calvert page includes holdings, key facts, documents and pricing information.

fees.note: As an ETF, the Calvert responsible-index product is generally cheaper than many active responsible mutual funds.

accessibility.note: ETF structure makes access comparatively straightforward through brokerage platforms, subject to local availability.

products.name: iShares ESG MSCI KLD 400 ETF (DSI)
products.description: A long-running social-index ETF that is more values-aware than a plain index, but still weighted toward large mainstream public companies.

environment.note: The iShares fund tracks the MSCI KLD 400 Social Index, which screens companies by ESG criteria rather than by full fossil-free divestment alone.

ethics.note: The fund gives exposure to the KLD social index, but users should still inspect holdings because index ESG criteria may not match personal values.

transparency.note: BlackRock publishes daily fund data, holdings, documents, factsheets and ESG characteristics for DSI.

fees.note: The fact sheet lists a higher expense ratio than the cheapest broad-market ETFs but still low relative to many active funds.

accessibility.note: As a large iShares ETF, DSI is easy to buy through many US brokerage accounts.

products.name: L&G Future World ESG Developed Index Fund
products.description: A low-cost UK developed-markets ESG index option, useful for broad exposure but still lighter-touch than specialist impact funds.

environment.note: The fund tracks a Solactive/L&G enhanced ESG developed-markets benchmark rather than an unscreened developed-market index.

ethics.note: The ESG tilt improves on a plain tracker but is not the same as strict ethical exclusion or targeted impact investing.

transparency.note: L&G and retail platforms publish fund documents, index objective, factsheets and charges for inspection.

fees.note: UK platform data shows low ongoing charges compared with active sustainability funds.

accessibility.note: The fund is available through some UK retail platforms, though not as universally portable as a major global ETF.

products.name: Nest Ethical Fund
products.description: An ethical opt-in fund inside the UK Nest workplace pension system, important because pension defaults are where many people can move real money.

environment.note: Nest describes the Ethical Fund as designed for members concerned about the social and environmental impact of the organisations they invest in.

ethics.note: Nest says the Ethical Fund avoids sectors such as animal-tested cosmetics, fur, tobacco, alcohol, pornography and gambling.

transparency.note: Nest publishes quarterly investment reports and fund factsheets so members can inspect where funds are invested.

fees.note: Nest says all its funds have the same low charges applied, so the ethical option is not penalized with a separate high charge.

accessibility.note: The ethical fund is available to Nest members as an opt-in choice, but not to people outside the Nest pension system.

products.name: Aviva Stewardship Funds
products.description: A workplace-pension fund range using stewardship pillars and exclusion screens, but still requiring users to check the specific fund and charges.

environment.note: Aviva says the Stewardship Funds are built around the sustainability pillars Climate, Earth and People.

ethics.note: Aviva's current Stewardship page says screens exclude businesses and sectors deemed harmful, while investments must contribute to Climate, Earth or People pillars.

transparency.note: Aviva publishes the Stewardship philosophy and fund-centre materials, though the user still has to inspect the specific pension fund.

fees.note: Charges vary by pension arrangement and fund, so fees are less straightforward than a single retail ETF expense ratio.

accessibility.note: The Stewardship funds are available through Aviva workplace pensions, making access dependent on employer and scheme menu.

products.name: J.P. Morgan Personal Investing SRI (formerly Nutmeg)
products.description: A hands-off UK managed portfolio route, formerly Nutmeg, for investors who want an SRI option without choosing individual funds.

environment.note: J.P. Morgan Personal Investing says its SRI style prioritises ESG leaders while limiting companies involved in controversial activities; it is not a strict fossil-free mandate.

ethics.note: The current SRI description says the style leans toward higher ESG standards while avoiding some problematic sectors and behaviours.

transparency.note: J.P. Morgan's SRI guide explains how the portfolios are scored under ESG regulation and discusses performance and greenwashing safeguards.

fees.note: The current fee schedule puts Socially Responsible Investing in the managed style fee band: 0.75% on the first GBP100k and 0.35% above that, before fund costs/spreads.

accessibility.note: The service now presents itself as J.P. Morgan Personal Investing, noting that Nutmeg users are now on the J.P. Morgan Personal Investing platform.

products.name: Moneyfarm ESG portfolios
products.description: A managed ETF-portfolio option that makes ESG investing easy, with clearer pricing than many advisers but lighter values depth than specialist funds.

environment.note: Moneyfarm says its ESG portfolios use ESG ETFs to build diversified portfolios with a greater sustainability focus.

ethics.note: Moneyfarm says its ESG strategy uses ETF-selection and portfolio-exposure checks, but there is no single definitive ESG standard, so users should inspect underlying ETFs.

transparency.note: Moneyfarm explains its ESG portfolio approach and publishes pricing, though underlying ETF holdings still need separate review.

fees.note: Moneyfarm publishes tiered management fees plus average fund costs and market-spread effects on its ESG page.

accessibility.note: The managed-portfolio flow is easier than selecting funds manually, but availability is limited to Moneyfarm markets and account types.

products.name: iShares U.S. Carbon Transition Readiness ETF (LCTU)
products.description: A mainstream U.S. equity ETF tilted toward companies BlackRock scores as better prepared for the low-carbon transition, but not a fossil-free impact fund.

environment.note: The fund targets U.S. companies assessed for carbon-transition readiness rather than applying a strict fossil-free exclusion.

ethics.note: Climate-transition scoring is narrower than a broad impact or justice screen, so ethics fit depends on the current holdings.

transparency.note: iShares publishes portfolio characteristics, performance, holdings and prospectus materials on the fund page.

fees.note: BlackRock lists a 0.30% gross expense ratio and 0.15% net expense ratio for LCTU on the fund page.

accessibility.note: As an ETF, it is broadly accessible through brokerage accounts, subject to the user's jurisdiction and platform.

products.name: Xtrackers S&P 500 Scored & Screened ETF (SNPE)
products.description: A low-cost S&P 500 screened ETF: easier and cheaper than many ESG products, but still a light screen on a mainstream large-cap index.

environment.note: The fund tracks a scored and screened S&P 500 exposure, which is materially weaker than a fossil-free or impact mandate.

ethics.note: The screen is useful but broad-market oriented; users should verify holdings rather than treating the ESG label as a values guarantee.

transparency.note: DWS publishes fund facts, portfolio, pricing details and documents for the ETF.

fees.note: DWS lists SNPE with a 0.10% expense ratio, making it a relatively low-cost screened option.

accessibility.note: It is a U.S.-listed ETF and therefore generally easy to buy through U.S. brokerage accounts.

products.name: Vanguard Baillie Gifford Global Positive Impact Stock Fund
products.description: A U.S. mutual fund wrapper for Baillie Gifford's positive-impact strategy, with stronger impact intent than ESG-light funds but active-fund costs.

environment.note: The annual impact report says the fund seeks capital appreciation with emphasis on businesses contributing to a more sustainable and inclusive world.

ethics.note: The strategy is explicitly built around positive change themes, rather than only excluding a few controversial sectors.

transparency.note: Vanguard publishes the fund profile, documents and shareholder reporting, including Baillie Gifford impact reporting.

fees.note: As an actively managed impact mutual fund, it is not in the ultra-low-cost index-fund bucket; investors should check current expenses before buying.

accessibility.note: Vanguard's U.S. mutual fund platform improves access compared with some boutique impact funds, but availability still depends on brokerage and account type.

products.name: Baillie Gifford Positive Change Fund
products.description: A concentrated active fund that invests in companies intended to contribute to social or environmental solutions, with impact reporting and active-fund tradeoffs.

environment.note: The fund objective includes contributing to a more sustainable and inclusive world through companies addressing social or environmental challenges.

ethics.note: Baillie Gifford describes four positive-change areas including social inclusion, environment and resource needs, healthcare and base-of-pyramid needs.

transparency.note: The fund page publishes documents, portfolio information and an impact-reporting framework.

fees.note: Baillie Gifford lists the B Acc share class ongoing charge at 0.53%, reasonable for active impact but higher than cheap ETFs.

accessibility.note: Direct share-class minimums can be high, although platform access may have different limits.

products.name: FP WHEB Sustainability Impact Fund
products.description: A specialist impact fund focused on companies selling products and services tied to sustainability challenges, with unusually explicit impact tools.

environment.note: WHEB says the fund focuses on opportunities created by transition to healthy, zero-carbon and sustainable economies.

ethics.note: The fund invests in companies selling products and services that help meet social and environmental challenges.

transparency.note: WHEB publishes reports, impact tools, portfolio-company views and voting records for the strategy.

fees.note: It is a premium active impact fund; investors should read the current KIID/prospectus and costs before buying.

accessibility.note: The fund is a UK/EU-style OEIC/UCITS product, so access is narrower than a U.S.-listed ETF.

products.name: Liontrust Sustainable Future funds
products.description: A UK sustainable-investment fund range using Liontrust's Sustainable Future process across equity, bond and managed portfolios.

environment.note: Liontrust describes the Sustainable Future process as finding opportunities for sustainable investing across multiple funds.

ethics.note: The range is built around sustainability themes and exclusions rather than only generic ESG scoring.

transparency.note: Liontrust publishes SFDR and fund reporting for environmental/social characteristics and sustainable-investment goals.

fees.note: These are active managed funds, so they are generally not as cheap as passive index ETFs; check each share class.

accessibility.note: UK platform availability is better than boutique private investments, but it is still not a globally accessible ETF.

products.name: AXS Green Alpha ETF (NXTE)
products.description: A fossil-free ETF managed around Green Alpha's next-economy thesis, higher conviction than broad ESG screens but narrower and more active.

environment.note: Green Alpha describes its portfolios as fossil-fuel free and says it avoids fossil extractors, suppliers and major demand drivers.

ethics.note: The ETF targets companies Green Alpha identifies as enabling a more sustainable next economy, a narrower impact thesis than standard ESG.

transparency.note: AXS publishes ETF facts and documents, and Fossil Free Funds independently shows no fossil holdings in the latest filing it reports.

fees.note: This is an active thematic ETF, so costs are likely higher than broad passive ESG index funds.

accessibility.note: As a U.S.-listed ETF, it is more accessible than private impact deals but still narrower than major index ETFs.

products.name: Impax Global Women's Leadership Fund
products.description: A gender-lens global equity fund that weights companies using women's leadership criteria rather than a pure climate mandate.

environment.note: This is primarily a women's-leadership and gender-lens strategy, so climate value is indirect rather than the core mandate.

ethics.note: Impax presents the strategy as gender-lens investing focused on companies with stronger women's leadership characteristics.

transparency.note: The fund page publishes AUM, holdings range, documents and strategy information.

fees.note: Public market data lists investor-class net expense ratio around the high end for index-like exposure, so fees are not the strength.

accessibility.note: The fund is available for sale in the United States with a stated minimum investment, making it more accessible than private impact products.

products.name: The Big Exchange
products.description: A UK investment platform that rates funds for positive impact before listing them, making ethical fund discovery easier for ordinary savers.

environment.note: The platform actively rates funds for positive impact on people and planet before making them available.

ethics.note: The Big Exchange exists to help users match investments with values, but the underlying fit still depends on the chosen fund.

transparency.note: It provides an explicit positive-impact rating layer alongside fund selection, making comparison easier than ordinary fund supermarkets.

fees.note: The platform states a 0.25% per annum platform fee, with fund-manager fees still applying.

accessibility.note: It is designed as an online UK impact-investing platform, easier than direct private deals but not globally available.

products.name: Ethex
products.description: A UK platform for direct positive investments into community energy, affordable housing, sustainable farming and other mission-led organisations.

environment.note: Ethex reports raising money for community energy, sustainable farming and other projects creating a fairer, more sustainable future.

ethics.note: Ethex says it helps everyday people make ethical investments that fund UK organisations with social and environmental missions.

transparency.note: Project-level offers can be clear, but direct crowdfunding investments are not as diversified or standardized as public funds.

fees.note: Ethex says setting up an account and accessing some managed investments is free; individual offers may have their own costs or payment fees.

accessibility.note: The platform is UK-focused and direct positive investments can be illiquid and higher risk than listed funds.

products.name: Abundance Investment
products.description: A UK platform for direct green and social investments, including council green loans and projects tied to local net-zero work.

environment.note: Abundance's council page describes green and social loans accredited against Green & Social Loan Principles.

ethics.note: The platform's Green & Social Finance Framework is intended to align council borrowing with green and social loan principles.

transparency.note: Project and framework disclosures are stronger than generic ESG labels, but investments are still project-specific and risky.

fees.note: Abundance's model is issuer-funded for many offers, but users must read each investment's costs and risk terms.

accessibility.note: Abundance says everyone can get involved and invest from GBP 5, but it is UK-focused and capital is at risk.

products.name: Oikocredit
products.description: A long-running social-impact investor supporting financial inclusion, agriculture and renewable energy partners, with a cooperative impact-first identity.

environment.note: Oikocredit lists renewable energy as one of its three focus sectors, alongside financial inclusion and agriculture.

ethics.note: Oikocredit says investments support local partners providing financial services, agriculture and renewable energy opportunities to empower communities.

transparency.note: Oikocredit publishes social impact reporting, including partner financing and focus-sector information.

fees.note: This is not a low-cost public index fund; investors must check local offering documents, risks and costs before committing money.

accessibility.note: Oikocredit is internationally known, but actual investor eligibility and product terms depend on local support associations and regulations.

products.name: CREF Responsible Balanced Account
products.description: A TIAA workplace-retirement variable-annuity option, formerly CREF Social Choice Account, built around ESG leadership and impact fixed income inside a balanced allocation.

environment.note: TIAA says CREF Social Choice was renamed CREF Responsible Balanced to better reflect the account's ESG-focused investment strategy.

ethics.note: TIAA's responsible-investing materials describe the account as combining ESG leadership with social and environmental impact fixed income.

transparency.note: TIAA publishes factsheets for CREF account classes, but actual terms depend on the employer plan and share class.

fees.note: CREF account costs vary by class and plan; the user should read the plan factsheet rather than assuming a single public expense ratio.

accessibility.note: This is most relevant for participants whose employer retirement menu already uses TIAA/CREF accounts, not a universal brokerage product.

products.name: BlackRock LifePath ESG Index funds
products.description: A mainstream target-date ESG index series for retirement menus, useful as an easy default but not a strict fossil-free choice.

environment.note: BlackRock says the funds optimize exposure to higher ESG ratings while seeking risk/return characteristics similar to parent indexes, which is a tilt rather than a fossil-free screen.

ethics.note: The strategy is an ESG index target-date approach, so its values fit depends on the underlying index methodology and holdings.

transparency.note: BlackRock product pages publish fund approach, holdings, characteristics and documents for the target-date series.

fees.note: As an index target-date series, this is generally positioned as a lower-cost retirement default than active ESG advice, but class fees must be checked.

accessibility.note: Target-date funds are common employer-plan defaults; availability depends on whether the plan menu includes this ESG series.

products.name: Fidelity International Sustainability Index Fund
products.description: A Fidelity index fund for non-U.S. equity exposure using a sustainability/ESG international benchmark rather than a plain unscreened international index.

environment.note: Fidelity identifies FNIDX as an international sustainability index fund; users still need to inspect holdings for fossil-fuel and bank exposure.

ethics.note: Fidelity Charitable describes the related sustainable international index exposure as tracking an MSCI ACWI ex USA ESG index.

transparency.note: Fidelity publishes holdings, prospectus, reports and related literature for the fund.

fees.note: This is an index-style fund, which generally keeps costs lower than active international ESG funds, but investors should check the current share-class expense ratio.

accessibility.note: Fidelity mutual funds are broadly brokerage-accessible in the U.S., though retirement-plan availability depends on the menu.

products.name: iShares ESG Aware MSCI EAFE ETF
products.description: A large, easy-to-buy international developed-markets ESG ETF that keeps the tradeoff visible: broad access and low cost, but relatively light ESG screening.

environment.note: iShares says ESGD targets ESG characteristics in aggregate while seeking similar risk and return to the MSCI EAFE Index, which implies a tilt rather than strict exclusion.

ethics.note: The ETF's stated approach is ESG-aware international exposure, not a dedicated impact or justice mandate.

transparency.note: iShares publishes fund holdings, documents, sustainable screens and characteristics on the product page.

fees.note: The iShares fact sheet lists a 0.20% expense ratio for ESGD, placing it in low-cost ETF territory for international ESG exposure.

accessibility.note: As a U.S.-listed ETF, ESGD is easy to buy through many brokerages, subject to ordinary ETF trading risks and account availability.

products.name: SPDR MSCI USA Gender Diversity ETF
products.description: A gender-diversity ETF focused on U.S. large and mid-cap companies with higher representation of women in leadership and workforce metrics.

environment.note: The fund is not primarily a climate screen; State Street's fund page still shows sector exposure including energy.

ethics.note: State Street says the fund tracks an index of companies showing commitment to gender diversity across board, senior management and workforce levels.

transparency.note: The product page publishes benchmark, holdings, documents and fund characteristics, making the gender-lens screen inspectable.

fees.note: State Street lists a 0.20% gross expense ratio for SHE.

accessibility.note: SHE is a U.S.-listed ETF on NYSE Arca, making it brokerage-accessible for many U.S. investors.

products.name: Ellevest Wealth Management impact portfolios
products.description: A women-led wealth-management route that can personalize impact portfolios across public equities, fixed income and alternatives, but with high minimums.

environment.note: Ellevest describes climate-conscious impact portfolios using criteria around water, carbon footprint, sustainable agriculture, pollution and deforestation.

ethics.note: Ellevest says its impact work can include intentional impact portfolios, municipal impact bonds and private alternatives aligned to client goals.

transparency.note: Ellevest publishes wealth-management methodology, Form ADV/CRS links and impact-investing explanations, but portfolio details are client-specific.

fees.note: Ellevest lists AUM fees from 0.35% to 1.25%, making it much costlier than low-fee index funds.

accessibility.note: Ellevest says full wealth management is for clients with $500,000 or more to invest, which sharply limits access.

products.name: EarthFolio SRI portfolios
products.description: An online managed SRI portfolio service using sustainable mutual funds, including fossil-free portfolio options for investors who want a managed route.

environment.note: EarthFolio says its fossil-free portfolios exclude companies engaged in exploration, production or distribution of coal, oil and natural gas.

ethics.note: EarthFolio says its portfolios use sustainable funds screened on up to ten environmental, social and governance criteria.

transparency.note: The service explains broad sustainability criteria and fossil-free definitions, but users still need underlying fund holdings and advisory documents.

fees.note: EarthFolio's FAQ lists a 0.50% annual management fee, with a flat quarterly fee when balances fall below the minimum.

accessibility.note: EarthFolio's FAQ says the minimum to open or maintain an account is $25,000, limiting access compared with no-minimum ETFs.

products.name: Carbon Collective ClimateSmart portfolios
products.description: A climate-focused advisory and retirement-plan route that excludes fossil-fuel-dependent sectors, overweights climate solutions, and also warns that the strategy can diverge from ordinary index returns.

environment.note: Carbon Collective describes ClimateSmart as cutting fossil-fuel-dependent sectors and reinvesting that share into climate solutions.

ethics.note: The firm frames the strategy around climate risk and opportunity rather than generic ESG, with individual, 401(k)/403(b) and endowment routes.

transparency.note: Carbon Collective publishes portfolio breakdown, pricing, legal disclosures and SEC adviser-registration references.

fees.note: For individual accounts, Carbon Collective lists 1.00% on the first $5,000, 0.25% above that, plus underlying fund fees around 0.40%.

accessibility.note: The individual program says it has no account minimum, while workplace access depends on whether an employer adds the ClimateSmart option.

products.name: PensionBee Climate Portfolio (US IRA)
products.description: A US IRA rollover route with a climate-focused model portfolio, useful for people consolidating old 401(k)s or IRAs who want a managed sustainability option.

environment.note: PensionBee says the US Climate Portfolio aligns with Paris/Kyoto climate goals and invests in ETFs focused on the lower-carbon transition.

ethics.note: The portfolio is climate-focused rather than a broad social screen, with 80% equity and 20% income exposure through State Street ETFs.

transparency.note: The page names the ETF building blocks, risk level, allocation and adviser disclosures, so the route is more inspectable than a generic ESG label.

fees.note: PensionBee's US fee page lists the Climate Portfolio at a 0.85% annual wrap fee, with ETF fees included in the wrap fee.

accessibility.note: The US service is built around rolling old 401(k)s and IRAs into an app-managed IRA, with no opening, transfer, contribution or distribution fee listed.

products.name: PensionBee Climate Plan (UK)
products.description: A UK pension-plan option that tracks a Paris-aligned index and excludes fossil fuel producers, with a simple pension-platform experience.

environment.note: PensionBee says the UK Climate Plan tracks a Paris-aligned index, excludes fossil fuel producers and tilts toward lower carbon emissions.

ethics.note: The plan is primarily a climate and fossil-producer exclusion route, not a full-spectrum ethical screen across every social issue.

transparency.note: PensionBee publishes allocation by asset type and region for the plan and identifies State Street Investment Management as the data provider.

fees.note: The UK Climate Plan page lists one annual fee of 0.75%, halved on the portion of balances above GBP100,000.

accessibility.note: PensionBee presents the plan as a selectable UK pension option and publishes FCA-regulated, capital-at-risk disclosures on the page.

products.name: Wealthify Ethical Investing Plans
products.description: A mainstream UK app route for ethical stocks and shares ISAs, pensions and general investing, using screened funds rather than a fully fossil-free mandate.

environment.note: Wealthify says some Ethical Plan funds may still hold oil, gas or integrated energy companies, while excluding more harmful activities such as thermal coal and tar sands.

ethics.note: The Ethical Plans aim to exclude tobacco, gambling, controversial weapons and adult entertainment, subject to a stated 10% tolerance used by fund providers.

transparency.note: Wealthify explains its fund-provider selection, screening tolerances, PRI signatory preference and the limits of its ethical approach.

fees.note: Wealthify lists a 0.6% annual management fee plus approximately 0.58% fund and trading fees for Ethical Plans.

accessibility.note: The product is presented as an app and dashboard route with five Ethical Investing Plans and the ability to change investment style.

products.name: Wahed halal portfolios
products.description: A Shariah-compliant digital investment route for investors whose values screen must include riba, financial-ratio and haram-industry constraints that ordinary ESG often misses.

environment.note: Wahed frames its portfolios around Shariah compliance rather than climate impact, so environmental fit depends on the selected holdings and risk profile.

ethics.note: Wahed explains that halal investing screens out riba, conventional finance, gambling, tobacco, adult entertainment, weapons and other haram activities.

transparency.note: Wahed says Shariah compliance is guided by its Shariah Supervisory Board and disclosed screening methodologies, with SEC adviser disclosures for the US entity.

fees.note: Wahed's pricing page shows an estimated wrap-fee structure of 0.49% plus $60 per year for balances under $100,000 and 0.49% above $100,000.

accessibility.note: Wahed positions the service as a digital robo-advisor and says portfolios are recommended after a suitability questionnaire in the app.

products.name: Ethic personalized portfolios
products.description: A values-personalization and tax-smart portfolio platform used through advisors and institutions, strong for customization but not a self-serve low-fee route.

environment.note: Ethic says it uses sustainability research, data science and client priorities to translate values into portfolios, rather than offering one fixed climate fund.

ethics.note: Ethic's platform supports personalized, values-aligned investing through direct index, model portfolio and unified managed account routes.

transparency.note: Ethic describes reporting across financials, impact, tax and proxy voting, and states it manages over $8 billion for 300+ advisory and institutional firms.

fees.note: Ethic is accessed through advisors and institutions, so end-client costs depend on advisory arrangements rather than a simple public retail fee.

accessibility.note: The service is built for RIAs, family offices and institutions, which makes it less accessible than direct retail ETFs or no-minimum robo-advisors.

products.name: Newday Impact portfolios
products.description: A US impact-only asset manager using SDG and ESG principles, nonprofit partnerships and thematic portfolio construction; better as an impact route than a bargain index substitute.

environment.note: Newday says its portfolios address major ethical issues using UN Sustainable Development Goals and ESG principles, including environmental themes.

ethics.note: Newday describes itself as an impact-only asset manager and says it partners with conservation and development organizations to deliver impact outcomes.

transparency.note: The site links Form ADV, CRS and disclosures and describes a repeatable process, but detailed holdings and fees require advisory documents.

fees.note: Newday's disclosure language tells investors to consider Newday fees and custodial fees, but the public page does not present a simple retail fee table.

accessibility.note: Newday says advisory services are available only to US residents in jurisdictions where it is registered and brokerage is through Schwab.

products.name: Earth Equity fossil-free portfolios
products.description: A US sustainable-investment adviser whose fossil-free portfolios and Impact X-Ray fit people moving larger portfolios away from fossil fuels and other conflict exposures.

environment.note: Earth Equity says fossil-fuel-free is the only portfolio approach it offers, with Green Sage and other portfolios focused on sustainable solutions.

ethics.note: Earth Equity says its Impact X-Ray highlights fossil fuels, weapons, tobacco and other questionable companies in a portfolio.

transparency.note: The Green Sage page lists portfolio themes such as alternative energy, efficiency, water, green finance and community investments.

fees.note: The public pages emphasize advisor-managed portfolios rather than a simple low-cost retail ETF fee, so cost certainty is limited before adviser review.

accessibility.note: Earth Equity's Impact X-Ray prompt targets portfolios over $250,000, making this route less accessible than consumer apps or ETFs.

products.name: CIRCA5000 impact ETFs
products.description: A set of UK-listed thematic impact ETFs from CIRCA5000; the direct app route shut down, so this is best understood as ETF access through platforms, not a live consumer app.

environment.note: ETF Stream reported five CIRCA5000 UCITS ETFs across clean water, green energy, health, social empowerment and sustainable food/biodiversity themes.

ethics.note: CIRCA5000 described the range as Article 9 SFDR impact ETFs using impact reports, governance filters and controversy screening.

transparency.note: Crowdcube's company page says CIRCA5000 listed five London Stock Exchange ETFs and presented itself as a pure-impact ETF issuer.

fees.note: ETF Stream reported the initial ETF range with a 0.49% total expense ratio, cheaper than many active impact funds but costlier than plain index funds.

accessibility.note: Investment Week reported in 2024 that CIRCA5000 would shut its platform business and transfer clients to AJ Bell while focusing on its ETFs.

products.name: TreasuryDirect savings bonds
products.description: A direct U.S. Treasury route for I Bonds and EE Bonds: transparent, low-fee and useful for cash-like goals, but not a targeted climate or social-impact investment.

environment.note: Savings bonds avoid corporate holdings but finance the general U.S. government rather than a dedicated climate or fossil-free mandate.

ethics.note: The value fit is public-debt transparency and household access, not an explicit ethical screen or community-investment use of proceeds.

transparency.note: TreasuryDirect publishes current EE and I Bond rates, purchase rules, holding periods and redemption limits.

fees.note: TreasuryDirect says there is no charge to open or manage an account and that it adds no fee beyond the securities purchased.

accessibility.note: Savings bonds can be bought electronically from $25, but users need a TreasuryDirect account, U.S. address, taxpayer ID and bank account.

products.name: TreasuryDirect Treasury bills, notes and TIPS
products.description: A low-fee way to buy U.S. Treasury marketable securities directly at auction, useful for short-duration or inflation-aware savings but not values-screened.

environment.note: Treasury bills, notes, bonds, FRNs and TIPS finance general government borrowing rather than earmarked environmental projects.

ethics.note: The ethical fit is safety, liquidity and public auction transparency; it does not screen uses of federal spending by issue area.

transparency.note: Treasury publishes auction schedules, announcements, data and results for marketable securities.

fees.note: TreasuryDirect says the platform is free with no fees regardless of investment size.

accessibility.note: Treasury notes list a $100 minimum purchase in $100 increments, and marketable securities can be bought through TreasuryDirect or brokers.

products.name: IMPACT by Interactive Brokers
products.description: A brokerage app and dashboard that lets users choose values, flag conflicting companies and swap toward better-aligned holdings, stronger as a tool than as a managed impact fund.

environment.note: IBKR says IMPACT lets investors select values such as clean water and greenhouse-emissions exclusions, then view portfolio alignment.

ethics.note: The app supports 13 impact values and avoid lists for practices users find objectionable, making values alignment explicit.

transparency.note: Interactive Brokers publishes IMPACT feature explanations and states the impact dashboard uses third-party ESG data sources.

fees.note: IBKR markets IMPACT with commission-free trading for U.S. stocks and ETFs for new U.S. IMPACT users, subject to product disclosures.

accessibility.note: The service is app-based and available through Interactive Brokers accounts, but it expects self-directed stock and ETF decision-making.

products.name: Impact Shares ETFs
products.description: A small ETF family built with nonprofit partners such as NAACP, YWCA and UNCDF, useful when a social-issue screen matters more than pure lowest cost.

environment.note: The Impact Shares lineup is primarily organized around partner-defined social criteria, so climate fit varies by ETF rather than being universal.

ethics.note: Impact Shares says nonprofit partners define social criteria for each ETF to align corporate behavior with social values.

transparency.note: Fund pages and prospectus materials explain partner nonprofit criteria, holdings caveats, risk factors, charges and expenses.

fees.note: SEC prospectus filings show management fees around 0.49% to 0.75%, higher than broad low-cost index ETFs.

accessibility.note: The funds trade as ETFs on public exchanges, making them more accessible than private impact deals but narrower than mainstream index funds.

products.name: SoFi Automated Investing - Sustainable portfolio
products.description: A mainstream robo-advisor route with a sustainable portfolio option, good for ease but a lighter values fit than explicit fossil-free or impact funds.

environment.note: SoFi describes its Sustainable automated portfolio as socially responsible and eco conscious, using ESG-characteristic companies rather than a strict fossil-free rule.

ethics.note: The portfolio is a mainstream automated option with ESG framing, so social impact depends on underlying portfolio construction and disclosures.

transparency.note: SoFi publishes automated-investing pricing and disclosures, but detailed values fit still requires reading portfolio and advisory documents.

fees.note: SoFi's pricing page lists a 0.25% annual robo-advisor management fee plus underlying investment expenses.

accessibility.note: The automated-investing product is built for beginner and hands-off investors and lists a low starting minimum in public pricing materials.

products.name: Acorns ESG portfolios
products.description: A beginner-friendly round-up investing app with ESG model portfolios, easy to use but less compelling for small balances once flat monthly fees are counted.

environment.note: Acorns says ESG portfolios use ETFs that follow MSCI rules-based ESG methodology to identify industry leaders and laggards.

ethics.note: The ESG portfolios include environmental, social and governance criteria, but are still broad ETF portfolios rather than direct community impact.

transparency.note: Acorns publishes ESG portfolio ETF lists and Form CRS materials describing Core and ESG portfolio choices.

fees.note: Acorns subscription plans start at $3 per month, a flat fee that can be high as a percentage of small balances.

accessibility.note: Acorns is designed for automated beginner investing with round-ups, recurring contributions and bundled education.

products.name: Stash Smart Portfolio
products.description: A beginner-oriented automated portfolio inside Stash's subscription app, useful for hand-holding but not a purpose-built values or climate product.

environment.note: Stash describes Smart Portfolio around risk profile, diversification and long-term growth, not a default fossil-free or climate mandate.

ethics.note: Stash publishes SRI education, but Smart Portfolio itself is positioned as automated diversified investing rather than impact screening.

transparency.note: Stash explains that Smart Portfolio is managed by Stash, rebalanced and matched to risk profile, with account limits in support materials.

fees.note: Stash pricing lists subscription fees plus a 0.25% AUM advisory fee on Smart Portfolios with balances of $1,000 or more.

accessibility.note: Stash emphasizes beginner access, guided investing and automated portfolio management through its app.

products.name: M1 Finance custom pies
products.description: A self-directed brokerage built around custom allocation pies, useful for people who want to build their own values mix but not a values-screened service by default.

environment.note: M1 Pies let users add and remove slices, so climate alignment depends on the user's chosen ETFs and stocks rather than platform screening.

ethics.note: The platform gives allocation control but does not itself guarantee ESG, fossil-free or impact alignment.

transparency.note: M1's pie model makes target allocations visible and automates rebalancing toward chosen slices.

fees.note: M1 says self-directed brokerage accounts have no commission, trading or management fees, but platform, IRA and regulatory fees can apply.

accessibility.note: M1 markets automated, fractional-share investing for target allocations, but users must choose and maintain their own values strategy.

products.name: Public.com
products.description: A mainstream brokerage app with stocks, ETFs, Treasuries, bonds, crypto and options, better on transparency than some trading apps but not a managed values portfolio.

environment.note: Public offers broad market access, including ETFs and Treasuries, but the platform itself does not make a default fossil-free allocation.

ethics.note: Public provides safety labels and risk context for some stocks, but users remain responsible for selecting values-aligned holdings.

transparency.note: Public publishes fee schedules and order-routing disclosures, including PFOF details for some order types.

fees.note: Public states regular-hours U.S. listed stock and ETF trades are commission-free, while other fees and plan transaction fees can apply.

accessibility.note: Public is an app-based, self-directed brokerage with quick funding and broad asset access, making it easy but potentially over-broad.

products.name: Robinhood brokerage
products.description: A highly accessible trading app and honest floor for this lens: easy and low-friction, but weak on values screening and carrying significant conduct-history penalties.

environment.note: Robinhood offers broad self-directed trading rather than a default ESG or fossil-free investing path.

ethics.note: Robinhood Financial's April 2026 Form CRS says the firm and its financial professionals have legal or disciplinary history, so conduct-history risk remains a current caution.

transparency.note: Robinhood's April 2026 Form CRS discloses conflicts including payment for order flow, principal trading and affiliated products, but those conflicts keep transparency trust limited.

fees.note: Robinhood publishes trading-fee details and passes through some regulatory fees, with low visible commissions but other business-model tradeoffs.

accessibility.note: The app is designed for broad, mobile-first access to stocks, ETFs, options, crypto and related trading products.

products.name: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios
products.description: A major robo-advisor with no visible advisory fee and broad ETF diversification, useful for ease but not the strongest values route because ESG is not its core portfolio design.

environment.note: Schwab offers ESG fund research separately, but Intelligent Portfolios is described around diversified ETF portfolios rather than ESG defaults.

ethics.note: The service automates diversified investing but does not make a direct impact or fossil-free promise in the core product description.

transparency.note: Schwab publishes ETF asset-class guides, FAQs, historical-performance examples and disclosure language for the portfolio program.

fees.note: Schwab says there is no advisory fee or commissions, but investors pay ETF expenses and an indirect cost from portfolio cash allocation.

accessibility.note: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios requires a $5,000 minimum and a questionnaire-based setup, making it accessible but not no-minimum.

products.name: ScholarShare 529 ESG portfolios
products.description: A state 529 college-savings route with ESG enrollment-year portfolios, useful for families who want education savings with some ESG consideration.

environment.note: ScholarShare's ESG enrollment portfolios are intended for savers who prefer investments that give special consideration to ESG criteria.

ethics.note: The ESG option adds values consideration to college savings, though it remains a 529 plan portfolio rather than direct impact investing.

transparency.note: ScholarShare publishes portfolio pages with benchmarks, performance tables, inception dates and links to plan-description disclosures.

fees.note: The 2026/2027 Enrollment Portfolio ESG page lists total annual asset-based fees of 0.18%, with later enrollment-year ESG portfolios higher.

accessibility.note: A 529 plan is a specialized education-savings account with tax and qualified-expense rules, so it is not a general-purpose investing account.

products.name: Broad market index fund (e.g. S&P 500)
products.description: A low-cost unscreened market fund that buys the index, including companies a values investor may want to avoid.

environment.note: Broad index funds can hold fossil-fuel companies unless the index explicitly excludes them; Fossil Free Funds is built to inspect that exposure.

ethics.note: An unscreened broad index buys the market rather than applying values screens such as fossil-free, weapon-free, prison-free or tobacco-free filters.

transparency.note: Large index funds publish holdings and factsheets, making them inspectable even when they are not values-screened.

fees.note: Broad passive index funds are among the cheapest fund structures; Vanguard's 500 Index Fund Admiral Shares is a low-expense example.

accessibility.note: Broad index funds are widely available through brokerages and many retirement plans.

products.name: Mainstream 'ESG' fund
products.description: A mainstream ESG-labelled fund where the label may mean light tilts, best-in-class scoring, exclusions, or engagement.

environment.note: SEC guidance says ESG funds use different definitions, weights and strategies, so some still hold fossil-fuel companies.

ethics.note: ESG can mean exclusion, integration, best-in-class selection, engagement or marketing language; verify the method before trusting the label.

transparency.note: The key check is the fund's prospectus, holdings and methodology, not the ESG name.

fees.note: ESG funds can charge more than plain index funds; read the expense ratio rather than assuming a fair price.

accessibility.note: ESG-labelled funds are widely marketed and often easy to buy, which is separate from whether the screen is strong.

products.name: Actively-managed conventional fund
products.description: A traditional active fund that tries to beat a benchmark, usually without an explicit values screen.

environment.note: Without a published fossil-free or ESG screen, a conventional active fund may hold fossil-fuel companies; inspect holdings fund-by-fund.

ethics.note: A conventional active mandate is usually return/benchmark-focused unless the prospectus names explicit ethical exclusions or impact goals.

transparency.note: Mutual funds disclose objectives, risks, fees and periodic holdings, but not with the directness of a purpose-built impact product.

fees.note: Active management commonly costs more; fund expenses reduce investor returns and should be compared before buying.

accessibility.note: Active funds are common through advisers, brokerages and retirement menus, even when their values fit is weak.

products.name: Fossil-fuel / defense-heavy fund
products.description: A sector fund, theme fund, or unscreened product concentrated in fossil-fuel or weapons exposure: the honest floor for this lens.

environment.note: Fossil Free Funds identifies funds with direct fossil-fuel holdings; an energy-sector fund is intentionally exposed to that sector.

ethics.note: As You Sow maintains separate fund screens for weapons, prisons and other harms, which is exactly what this floor option fails.

transparency.note: Sector funds disclose holdings, but transparency does not make the underlying exposure values-aligned.

fees.note: Sector ETF costs vary by product; the user must compare expense ratios, trading costs and concentration risk.

accessibility.note: Sector ETFs are easy to buy through brokerages, which is why they deserve an explicit floor rather than omission.
